messages:
mira: Quick follow-up on the QKV fusion RFC. TL;DR — we need a small compatibility surface to let serving pick: fused QKV, split Q/K/V, or a dropout-free inference path that bypasses dropout layers. This is about rollout safety and perf regressions.

alex: +1. Can we define a narrow enum in the runtime config? e.g. `qkv_mode = {\"auto\", \"fused\", \"split\", \"fallback\"}` and `inference_dropout = \"off\"|\"on\"`?

sam: We should also include a kernel capability bitmap from the device probe so routing can prefer fused only when hw/kernel supports fused-bias+rope. otherwise fallback to split.

jen: Agree on bitmap. Also call out ABI: fused kernels must accept both (a) packed QKV contiguous layout and (b) legacy interleaved layout, or we need a narrow adapter that shuffles once at load time. Shuffling per request is too expensive.

mira: Good point. We probably want a one-time layout transform at model load for Dedicated/Private to avoid runtime CPU overhead. For Hosted API we can opt for on-the-fly transform with caching.

ryan: For the dropout-free path, let's be explicit: inference mode disables dropout ops and uses alternative scaling. Implementation note: some open models bake dropout semantics into training-time scaling; need to ensure numeric parity with eval sets.

alex: Rollout plan idea: start with `qkv_mode = auto` that picks fused when kernel capability & layout==packed. Add a `force_fused=true` flag behind an opt-in per-tenant. That lets us test perf while we monitor quality/regressions.

sam: Add metrics: `fusion_selected`, `fusion_shim_cost_ms`, `layout_transform_bytes`, and an eval metric that measures top-k token diffs against baseline split-kernel for a sampled prompt set.

jen: Contract for kernel authors: fused kernel must expose micro-benchmarks (latency, peak memory, token/s) and a deterministic fallback path when inputs contain NaNs/inf or odd sequence lengths. No silent truncation.

mira: Ops concerns: when fused kernel OOMs we need graceful fallback to split kernel with zero request loss. That implies the runtime must snapshot the KV cache and switch execution path mid-request or reject and retry with split. Which is less disruptive?

ryan: Prefer transparent retry within runtime: if kernel returns OOM sentinel synchronously, runtime launches split-kernel fallback and continues. Need to timebox to avoid cascading slowdowns.

alex: Implementation checklist (short):
```
- device capability probe (fused_bias, fused_rope, packed_qkv)
- model load layout transformer + cache
- qkv_mode config + per-tenant override
- runtime fallback on OOM with retry counter
- telemetry hooks + token-diff sampling
- rollout canary + opt-in tenants
```

mira: Tests we need: microbench on various seq-len distributions, large-batch stress test to exercise layout transformer, functional diffs on 1k eval prompts, and a chaos test that forces OOMs to validate fallback.

jen: One more: add a small compatibility header in model artifact metadata e.g. `supported_kernels: [\"fused_qkv_v1\", \"split_v2\"]` so model packaging can declare expectations.

sam: UX: console should show why fused wasn't chosen (capability mismatch, layout, tenant opt-out) so SRE can debug perf drops.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary build 2026.03.18-rc3 queued for eng-runtime/fused-qkv. Link: https://ci.internal/ci/3421 :white_check_mark:

mira: OK let's action: alex + sam to spec device probe & config enum PR; jen to draft kernel author contract; ryan to spec OOM retry behavior and timeboxing; I'll own rollout checklist and telemetry queries. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll open PRs today.

jen: Drafting contract, will ping kernel maintainers.

ryan: I'll add retry circuit in runtime and a test harness.

sam: Will prototype layout transformer and add metrics.

mira: Great — we'll sync next Wed to review canary results.
